title: Fluorescent Labeling of Reovirus with Succinimidyl Ester Dyes
author: Bernardo Mainou
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kqhcvt6

steps.title: Prepare bicarbonate buffer and dilute virus
steps.instruction: Dilute 3 × 10¹² reovirus particles in up to 495 µL fresh 0.05 M sodium bicarbonate (pH 8.5). Prepare sodium bicarbonate by making a 10× stock (0.5 M) with 0.42 g NaHCO₃ in 10 mL ddH₂O, then dilute to 1× (0.05 M) in ddH₂O and filter‑sterilize through a 0.2 µm filter.

substeps.instruction: Make 10× sodium bicarbonate stock (0.5 M) by dissolving 0.42 g NaHCO₃ in 10 mL ddH₂O
Dilute the 10× stock to 1× (0.05 M) in ddH₂O
Filter‑sterilize the 0.05 M buffer with a 0.2 µm filter
Dilute 3 × 10¹² reovirus particles in up to 495 µL of the filtered buffer

steps.title: Make 1 mM Alexa dye stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve succinimidyl‑ester Alexa fluor (e.g., Alexa 546, MW 1159.6) in dimethylformamide to a final concentration of 1 mM; for example, add 862 µL DMF to 1 mg dye.

steps.title: Add dye to virus solution
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of the 1 mM Alexa dye stock to the virus‑bicarbonate mixture, achieving a final dye concentration of ~10 µM.

steps.title: Incubate labeling reaction
steps.instruction: Rock the reaction mixture in the dark for 90 min at room temperature or 4 °C (both conditions work; 4 °C may improve virus stability).

steps.title: Dialyze labeled virus
steps.instruction: Dialyze the labeled virus using a 6–8 kDa molecular‑weight‑cut‑off membrane against PBS at 4 °C overnight, replacing the PBS after the first hour.

substeps.instruction: Replace PBS after the first hour of dialysis
